episodes.title: At the restaurant and bank
episodes.publisher_title: Dialog am Restaurant an op der Bank (A2)
episodes.guide: Follow the restaurant order, then listen for the choices made at the bank. Listen for final decisions rather than the first suggestion.

questions.prompt: What does the vegetarian customer choose?
questions.explanation: In the restaurant scene, he rules out meat and chooses pizza.

questions.prompt: Do they order a small or a large bottle of water?
questions.explanation: They choose a large bottle to share.

questions.prompt: Does the bank customer want a credit card immediately?
questions.explanation: In the bank scene, he declines a credit card for now.

episodes.title: Directions and train tickets
episodes.guide: Listen for an alternative route to the station, then a destination, fare and travel class. The dialogue's routes and prices are listening practice, not current travel information.
episodes.note_heading: Audio B — De Wee an en Zuchbilljee (4:29)

questions.prompt: How long is the suggested walk to the church?
questions.explanation: In the directions scene, walking to the church takes five minutes. Other times describe different parts of the journey.

questions.prompt: Where does the customer want to travel by train?
questions.explanation: At the ticket counter, the customer asks to travel to Amsterdam.

questions.prompt: Which travel class does the customer select?

episodes.title: Shops and opening hours
episodes.guide: Keep track of which person describes each place. Listen for weekday and weekend differences, especially half-hours and early closing.

questions.prompt: At what time does Sophie's bakery close on Saturday?
questions.explanation: Sophie says her bakery closes at one in the afternoon on Saturday.

questions.prompt: What are Marc's post-office hours on Saturday morning?
questions.explanation: Marc's post office opens from nine until noon on Saturday.

episodes.title: Describing a home
episodes.guide: There are two different homes. Separate the advantages and disadvantages in the voice message from the furnishings described in the second conversation.

questions.prompt: In the first part, how many bedrooms does the apartment have?
questions.explanation: The first apartment has two bedrooms, as well as an office.

questions.prompt: In the second part, how large is the apartment?
questions.explanation: The speaker in the second conversation describes a 60-square-metre apartment.

episodes.title: Household chores and a shared flat
episodes.guide: Compare Lisa's routine with Max's shared household. Listen for who lives alone, shared versus individual duties, and the appliances each home has.

questions.prompt: Does Max's shared flat have a dishwasher?
questions.explanation: Max explains that the flat has no dishwasher, so the residents share the washing-up.

questions.prompt: What is Max responsible for this week?
questions.explanation: His duty this week is emptying the bin and handling recycling. The duties rotate.

episodes.title: A reservation and a catering order
episodes.publisher_title: Reservatioun am Restaurant a beim Traiteur bestellen (A2)
episodes.guide: The first call reserves a restaurant table. The second orders catering for a retirement celebration. Keep the two group sizes and arrangements separate.

questions.prompt: For how many people is the restaurant table reserved?
questions.explanation: The restaurant reservation is for four people; fifty belongs to the later catering call.

questions.prompt: Where does the restaurant customer prefer to sit?
questions.explanation: The customer requests an indoor table by a window.

episodes.title: Getting to know someone
episodes.guide: Start here for an easier listening session. Follow two people's introductions and distinguish their names, countries, work and free-time activities.

questions.explanation: Fabio introduces himself as Italian and says he comes from Turin.

questions.prompt: How often does Raïda go swimming?
questions.explanation: She says she goes swimming twice a week.

episodes.title: Fixing an order and a bill
episodes.guide: Listen for the difference between what was ordered and what arrived. In the second scene, identify the mistakes on the bill and how they are resolved.

questions.prompt: Which soup did the customer originally order?
questions.explanation: The customer ordered vegetable soup but initially receives tomato soup.

questions.prompt: How many salads were ordered in the second scene?
questions.explanation: Two salads were ordered, but the original bill lists three.
